title: ARTERY: Fast Quantum Feedback using Branch Prediction
problem: Quantum feedback in dynamic circuits introduces significant latency because each feedback branch must wait for measurement results to propagate through classical decoding and control, blocking gate execution and degrading circuit fidelity. The dynamic nature of mid-circuit measurement prevents speculative execution under current quantum control hardware.
motivation: Dynamic quantum circuits increasingly rely on fast mid-circuit feedback for error correction and algorithm execution, but the latency of measurement-to-gate feedback (dictated by readout and classical processing) has become a critical performance limiter.
method: ARTERY predicts quantum measurement outcomes while they're still happening, using two signals: historical statistics (how often this measurement gave each result) and real-time pulse analysis (the shape of the measurement signal as it arrives). A branch predictor combines these signals into a single prediction that downstream gates can act on immediately. The hardware includes FPGA interconnects for fast communication, a trigger system for precise gate timing, and adaptive sampling to extract maximum information from the measurement pulse.
key_novelty: ARTERY brings classical branch prediction to quantum circuits by combining historical measurement statistics with real-time pulse-shape analysis, enabling quantum gates to speculatively start executing before mid-circuit measurement results are complete.
contributions: Reconciled branch predictor combining historical branch statistics with real-time readout-pulse trajectory prediction, achieving over 90% prediction accuracy.
2.07x speedup in quantum feedback latency over state-of-the-art methods.
1.24x fidelity improvement due to reduced gate blocking.
Scalable inter-FPGA backplane connection with a feedback trigger mechanism and adaptive pulse sampling for hardware bandwidth maximization.

metrics.accuracy: Over 90% branch prediction accuracy; 1.24x fidelity improvement

limitations: Misprediction correction overhead and its impact on circuit fidelity at scale are not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Branch prediction for quantum feedback acceleration
